scope: execution-required KVM qga reboot service-state diagnosis

findings.guest_result: The first retained post-reboot admin-console query showed `STATE : 1 STOPPED` with `WIN32_EXIT_CODE : 1067 (0x42b)`.

findings.command: sc start QEMU-GA; sc query QEMU-GA
findings.guest_result: A manual restart moved the service through `START_PENDING` and then to `STATE : 4 RUNNING`.

findings.command: virsh qemu-agent-command ...; virsh qemu-monitor-command ... --pretty '{"execute":"query-chardev"}'; virsh qemu-monitor-command ... --hmp 'info qtree'; direct AF_UNIX connect
findings.guest_result: The guest-side service stayed running after the manual restart.
findings.host_result: `query-chardev` changed `charchannel1` to `frontend-open=true`, `info qtree` changed the qga port to `guest on, host off`, but `guest-ping` still returned `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and direct host-side connect to the qga unix socket still returned `Connection refused`.

findings.guest_result: The retained System log query returned `The QEMU Guest Agent service terminated unexpectedly. It has done this 1 time(s).`

conclusion: The KVM qga blocker is now explicitly two-stage: a fresh reboot leaves the Windows `QEMU-GA` service stopped with exit code 1067 and a matching unexpected-termination System log entry, while a manual service restart only recovers the guest side to `frontend-open=true` / `guest on, host off` without restoring a usable host-side attach path.
